reason: Selected sections describe a fixed-model, failure-driven harness loop and its regression gate. The gate uses the held-out split for promotion, which limits claims of untouched generalization.

candidates.title: Propose bounded harness edits from observed execution failures
candidates.rule: For repeated terminal, repository-repair or application-agent tasks, tie small edits to recurring trace-level failures and promote them only after checking for regressions under the same model and evaluator.
candidates.passage: no promoted harness degrades either split.
candidates.finding: The complete Self-Harness loop improves final pass rates in all nine reported model–benchmark combinations. The paper connects retained edits to artifact creation, tool-error recovery and application-state retrieval; those individual changes are not all isolated by component ablations.
candidates.conditions: Model weights, tool set, decoding and evaluator stay fixed. The same model proposes edits to declared harness surfaces. Candidate evaluation uses repeated attempts and a non-regressive promotion rule.
candidates.limitations: The held-out split is consulted by the promotion gate, so it is not an untouched final test set. Baselines are intentionally minimal; gains need not transfer to mature harnesses. The inspected sections do not establish a matched-compute alternative or that pass-rate non-regression is sufficient for higher-stakes changes.
candidates.validation_test: Test bounded failure-driven edits against the unchanged harness and a matched-budget baseline. Keep a final evaluation set out of both the proposer and promotion gate, and check non-score requirements separately.

review_scope: Focused reading of abstract/introduction and selected main-text results, ablations and limitations; intervening sections, references and appendices were not comprehensively reviewed.
